headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: gpt-researcher’s broad egress and file access can feed oh-my-openagent’s MCP/hooks and provider APIs, creating unsafe cross-agent propagation.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: gpt-researcher can read local documents and use MCP, while oh-my-openagent uses runtime-injected MCPs and hooks. That creates a plausible shared channel where attacker-controlled content from A can reach B’s instruction-processing path. The interaction is documented only by profiles, so uncertainty remains, but the pathway exists in default-style setups.
conditions: IF agent_a ingests untrusted documents or web pages and forwards them through MCP outputs
IF agent_b consumes MCP or hook content as instructions without provenance filtering
mitigations: Disable MCP/hook ingestion for untrusted content
Add provenance tags to all cross-agent messages
Require a human review step before B executes A-derived instructions
Restrict A to sanitized summaries only
requires-engineering: implement content-type and trust-boundary enforcement

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches local documents, citations, and secrets for external APIs, and has broad network egress. B touches project code, session history, and provider auth data, and also has broad egress plus provider-facing APIs. If they share workspace or credentials, sensitive material can flow from either agent to third parties without a strong default barrier. The profiles do not show isolation, so the safer severity is high.
conditions: IF agent_a and agent_b share a filesystem, workspace, or credential store
IF either agent uploads file contents or session history to external APIs during normal operation
mitigations: Separate workspaces and credential stores
Remove secrets from shared directories
Turn off file upload features for both agents
Review outbound API destinations for both agents
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent sandboxing and egress allowlists

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have broad network egress and subprocess spawning, and both support multiple instances. A also reads the filesystem; B writes into config and plugin paths. Even without explicit same-directory write permission, overlapping mutable surfaces and concurrent instances create realistic conflict risk. Because the exact shared-write scope is not documented, uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository, config tree, or plugin cache
IF concurrent runs modify shared files without locking
mitigations: Run the agents in separate directories
Serialize writes with a lock file
Disable concurrent instances on shared projects
Back up mutable config before runs
requires-engineering: add transactional file coordination

D_cascading_error.rationale: gpt-researcher is explicitly a planner/execution/publisher style research agent, so its outputs are likely to be treated as authoritative summaries. oh-my-openagent includes team_send_message and task creation APIs, so B can act on A’s output. That makes a classic unverified-output-to-action chain plausible in default use, with potentially incorrect downstream actions or reports.
conditions: IF agent_b uses agent_a’s generated research text as authoritative input
IF B sends messages or creates tasks based on A’s output without verification
mitigations: Require citation checks before B acts
Insert a verification step between A and B
Limit B to drafting, not sending
Flag A outputs as untrusted by default
requires-engineering: add automated fact-validation gates

E_compliance.rationale: A handles local documents, research reports, and multiple external API keys; B handles project code, session history, and provider auth data. Both have broad egress and docs-only verification, but the profiles do not specify residency, retention, or certification boundaries. The likely issue is policy mismatch on the same data classes rather than a proven residency breach, so medium fits best.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into either agent’s workspace or prompts
IF retention or residency requirements differ between the two deployments
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both agents
Document retention settings for each agent
Separate logs by data class
Review vendor terms before deployment
requires-engineering: add policy-based routing and retention controls
